blocks.title: Card application failure playbook
rows: The submit phase is already submitting
Ignore the second click; one request leaves
A slow reply or a timeout
A client timer that aborts the request
Keep every field and offer a retry with the same key
Sign in again in a dialog, keep the fields in memory, resubmit with the same key
Map errors by name, focus the summary, use a new key for the corrected submit
Show what happens next, poll, and say the page can be closed
Open the verification step and come back to the same applicationId

blocks.text: A pending decision is where most designs submit twice: a refresh, a second tab or Back. With the confirmation built as a read, each is another read of the same record.

blocks.title: Scenario walkthrough: a pending decision and a refresh

steps.title: The reply says pending review
steps.text: The service returns application a_19 with status pending-review. The shell replaces the history entry with the status route and announces the status in the live region.

steps.title: The applicant refreshes
steps.text: The status route reads a_19 again and posts nothing. The fields are gone from memory, which is fine: the confirmation shows only the masked values in the record.

steps.title: A second tab opens the same route
steps.text: It reads the same record. There is no form on that route, so a second application cannot start from it.

steps.title: Polling backs off
steps.text: The page polls with growing intervals, pauses while the tab is hidden and reads once when the applicant comes back.

steps.title: The decision lands
steps.text: Status becomes approved with a creditLimit. The live region announces it, the screen lists the next steps, and Telemetry records outcome_shown with the elapsed time and no values.

blocks.alt: State diagram from editing to submitting, then to field errors, a failed submit with a retry, or the status route with approved, declined, pending review and verify identity outcomes.
blocks.caption: Outcome states: a retry keeps the key, field errors start a new attempt, and every decision is read on the status route.
blocks.fallbackText: Text fallback: Editing leads to submitting. Submitting can end in field errors, which return to editing with a new key; in a failed submit, which retries with the same key; or in the status route. On the status route the record shows approved, declined, pending review or verify identity, and pending review and verify identity later turn into approved or declined.

blocks.title: Card application tests that protect applicants
items: Double-click Submit during a slow reply; assert one request and one application.
Time out the first submit and retry; assert the same applicationId comes back.
Refresh the confirmation and open it in a second tab; assert no POST is sent.
Search logs, URLs, analytics payloads and both browser storages after a submit; assert no Social Security number, date of birth or income appears.
Run keyboard and screen-reader passes over the error summary, the field errors and the decision announcement.

blocks.text: These tests guard the two promises an applicant cannot check alone: one application per attempt, and no sensitive value outside the form.
